subject: Production: Nimbus Labs sustained tail latency — pressure valve runbook & exec alignment
messages:
From: Alice Porter <alice@nimblabs.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@nimblabs.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Production impact: sustained tail latency on batch endpoints

Hi Tessa —

We're seeing a sustained long-tail on our nightly batch runs against the redwood/prod model endpoints starting ~02:00 UTC. p50/p90 look fine but p99/p999 are elevated and we're losing throughput — jobs that used to finish in 40–60s are now completing in 6–12m, which is breaking our downstream aggregation window. We've attached a telemetry snapshot and the job ids in the attachment.

Immediate ask: can you confirm if there's any capacity throttling, concurrency cap, or queueing/backpressure policy active tonight for our Dedicated pool? This is customer-impacting; we need a short-term mitigation and a remediation plan.

Thanks,
Alice Porter
Head of Platform Engineering, Nimbus Labs
nimblabs.com

Attachments: nimblabs-telemetry-snapshot-20261112.json (telemetry JSON, 78KB)

Subject: Re: Production impact: sustained tail latency on batch endpoints

Hi Alice — thanks for the heads up and the telemetry. I'm escalating this now. Initial checks: no scheduled maintenance, no policy changes on your Dedicated pool, but we do see periodic backpressure events correlating with a spike of long-context requests from a small subset of jobs.

Next steps from our side (rapid triage):
- I'm attaching our "tail-pressure-runbook-v1.pdf" with immediate mitigation steps (short-term: reduce concurrency per-client; medium: route heavy tail jobs to a lower-seq-length optimized variant).
- Aditya, can you confirm whether any autoscaler activity or eviction occurred between 01:45–03:30 UTC?
- Marissa, looping you for exec visibility and to coordinate a 30-min sync with Nimbus.

We'll push a temporary per-tenant concurrency cap (non-disruptive) and monitor. Expecting an update within 30m. Apologies for the disruption — we know the aggregation windows are time-sensitive.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: sustained tail latency on batch endpoints

Quick update from infra: we see a burst of requests with >4k tokens, which causes KV cache pressure and longer per-token kernel selection times. Autoscaler fired but added GPU capacity after ~6 minutes due to placement lag; during that window the queue grew and the serving runtime applied backpressure and enforced our tenant-level concurrency cap (configured at 32 for this pool).

Logs (condensed):
- 2026-11-12T02:05:17Z request id=job-99872 ctx=nimblabs seq=4600 tokens -> kernel fallback -> cold KV miss
- 2026-11-12T02:06:03Z eviction triggered pool=dedicated-nimbus reason=placement-delay
- 2026-11-12T02:09:35Z autoscaler scale_up target=+2gpus status=pending

Immediate mitigations we can apply now (I'll action 1–2 within 15m):
1) Apply a temporary tenant concurrency cap = 12 for batch endpoints (will throttle new jobs but let in-flight finish).
2) Route requests with seq>1024 to a quantized variant optimized for long context (minor quality delta).
3) Enable prefix KV caching for repeated batched prefixes in today's job set.

I'll implement 1) and 3) now and report. Dev, please keep on-call looped for rollback if things regress.

— Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: playbook-action-items.txt (3 items)

Subject: Re: Production: Nimbus Labs sustained tail latency — pressure valve runbook & exec alignment

Alice / Carlos —

Thanks again for the quick report and patience. Summary of what we did and immediate outcome: 
- At 02:23 UTC we applied a temporary tenant concurrency cap = 12 and turned on prefix KV caching for the affected batch routes.
- We routed seq>1024 jobs to a quantized long-context variant flagged for Nimbus to keep throughput.
- Autoscaler completed placement at 02:32 UTC and added 2 GPUs to your pool; steady state achieved by 02:40 UTC.

Effect: p99 for the batch endpoint reduced from ~4.7m to ~58s within the 30m mitigation window. We continued monitoring for 12 hours and saw no reoccurrence. Attached is the short runbook and the telemetry snapshot we pulled post-mitigation.

Next steps (follow-up):
- We'll run a workload replay against a staging variant for the long-context jobs with your ops team this week (suggest Thu 2026-11-18).
- Product will propose a medium-term change: tenant-aware placement hints + earlier scaling thresholds for long-context-heavy tenants.
- I'll produce the 1-page exec note and loop in CRO/CTO today.

Apologies for the impact — we're prioritizing a durable remediation so this doesn't recur. Marissa and Aditya will be on the call to walk through what happened.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
